technology_name: Fungus-Derived Antimicrobial for Pharma and Agri Use: Diethyl Phthalate Extraction
institution: KSCSTE- Malabar Botanical Garden & Institute for Plant Sciences (MBGIPS)
problem_solved: The global threat of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) creating an urgent need for novel, bio-based, broad-spectrum therapeutic and agricultural agents.
description: A natural product-based innovation centered on the discovery of Diaporthe penetriteum, an endophytic fungus isolated from Lagenandra toxicaria that serves as a novel microbial source of diethyl phthalate. The fungus is cultured under controlled laboratory conditions, and its bioactive metabolites are extracted using an eco-friendly ethyl acetate process. High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) analysis confirmed diethyl phthalate as the active compound, marking its first reported extraction from this species. The extract demonstrates strong broad-spectrum antimicrobial efficacy against major human pathogens, including Staphylococcus aureus, Bacillus subtilis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and E. coli.
applications:
• Next-generation natural antibiotic formulations for human and animal healthcare

• Bio-based crop protectants and biopesticides for sustainable agricultural pest control

• Out-licensing pipelines for pharmaceutical companies targeting multi-drug resistant strains

• Commercialization of green, eco-friendly microbial metabolite extraction processes
